paper_metadata.title: Quantum Architecture Search for Quantum Monte Carlo Integration via Conditional Parameterized Circuits with Application to Finance

summary: The paper introduces conditional parameterized quantum circuits (CPQCs) generated via genetic quantum architecture search to approximate option payoff functions used inside amplitude estimation for quantum Monte Carlo pricing. In noiseless simulation, the trained PQCs (e.g., 8 parameters for the vanilla option case) produce CPQC implementations whose gate counts scale O(n) with discretization qubits, compared with O(n log n) for IBM’s quantum arithmetic method; for a basket option example with n=14 control qubits the CPQC requires 92 CNOTs and circuit depth 151. No real quantum hardware experiments or classical runtime comparisons are performed.

experiments.description: Genetically trained PQC for basket option payoff with variable weight parameter, demonstrating that the circuit can approximate the payoff for different basket weights and can be converted into a CPQC for use in amplitude estimation.

algorithm.variant: genetic structure-learning PQC with conditional parameterized quantum circuit (CPQC) encoding for variable-weight basket payoff
algorithm.ansatz: PQC with rotational encoding gates (RX, RY, RZ) and parameterized layers discovered via genetic architecture search
algorithm.optimizer: RMSProp (PennyLane) for parameters combined with genetic mutation/selection for circuit structure

key_results: Circuit approximates basket payoff across multiple weight settings (examples shown for w1=0, w1≈0.37, w1≈0.74).
Weight parameter encoded once in the circuit yet generalizes across payoff shapes.
Demonstrates feasibility of reusing trained PQC for different basket weights before conversion to CPQC.
